checks.rationale: The decomposition follows every main action block and retains all three illustrated first-well and second-well routes. Tagmentation and PCR each have three local single-well instances; neither shared caption is treated as a joint reaction. Both distributions genuinely produce separate preparations, whereas nuclear pooling and DNA-product pooling genuinely combine their respective inputs. The same boundary state is reused between adjacent actions. Lysis is retained inside each supported PCR preparation block, avoiding an invented isolated intermediate. The left Single cell/chromatin cartoon explains the target, with no arrow into the main suspension route. No unshown sequencing/data branch or reagent-only transformation is added.

card.description_verbatim:
Single-cell ATAC-Seq uses combinatorial cellular indexing to measure chromatin accessibility in thousands of single cells per assay. This avoids the need for compartmentalization of individual cells, which makes the system scalable to analyze thousands of cells at a time.
In this method nuclei are isolated and molecularly tagged in bulk with barcoded Tn5 transposases in wells. Nuclei are then pooled and a limited number redistributed into a second set of wells. A second barcode is then introduced during the PCR amplification step. The fragments are then pooled for library prep and sequencing.
